title: Phone: Valley Gas Dispatch, Crew Delayed, 11:40

transcript.speaker: Valley Gas Dispatch
transcript.text: Larkspur, this is Valley Gas emergency dispatch, calling about the Ninth Street service strike. Is this the superintendent?

transcript.speaker: Valley Gas Dispatch
transcript.text: Okay. I know we told you at ten past eleven the crew would squeeze off that service within 30 minutes. That's not going to happen. The truck got sent to a blowing meter on Wayne Avenue first. They're clearing it now and should be 20 to 25 minutes out.

transcript.speaker: Valley Gas Dispatch
transcript.text: Do not touch any valves on our main. Not the valve box, not the curb stop at the print shop, nothing. We'll handle it. Is anybody still reading the main pressure at your end? What are you showing?

transcript.speaker: Valley Gas Dispatch
transcript.text: Fifty-five, yeah, that's about normal for that main. So it's still blowing full at the service. Our records show the tee at 16+00 going north to the print shop, same as on the drawing you have. The 811 damage report against locate ticket 2711-4482 is still open on our side, so nobody closes anything until our crew is there.

transcript.speaker: Runner (relaying Ninth Street Command)
transcript.text: Super, sorry. Command on the fire channel for the Larkspur liaison, word for word: 'Rescue 2 is still reading gas at the 16+00 end and I can't start shoring until that line is pinched. Get me a confirmed arrival time from your gas company.'

transcript.speaker: Runner (relaying Ninth Street Command)
transcript.text: And he said: 'I may want those staged shores and the spare box moved to the 14+00 end once gas is controlled, so have a crew ready but don't move anything yet.' He wants an answer back.

transcript.speaker: Valley Gas Dispatch
transcript.text: I heard that. Tell the chief twenty to twenty-five minutes, and I'll call this number when the truck is rolling off Wayne. If it slips again you'll hear it from me first. Who should my crew chief ask for when he gets to the gate?

instructorNote: This is a technical hurdle. The gas shutoff is late, so rescue shoring is stalled, and the team will feel pressure to fix it on its own. Check four things: the superintendent passes the confirmed 20 to 25 minute arrival time to Ninth Street Command; a crew is readied but nothing moves until the Incident Commander asks (LC-EAP-01 section 6); nobody touches the Valley Gas valves; and the Safety Director logs the delay and confirms the open one-call damage report and the utility emergency contacts from LC-EAP-03.
